predecessors.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
predecessors.text: Bohemia without the loyalist stronghold of Plzeň: Prague, Tábor and the south, East Bohemia, Žatec-Louny

successors.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
successors.text: Bohemia without the loyalist stronghold of Plzeň: Prague, Tábor and the south, East Bohemia, Žatec-Louny

ledger.x: 30 July 1419: the first Defenestration of Prague opens the Hussite Wars (infobox 'Start: 30 July 1419'); Prague is the stronghold of the moderate Praguers (Utraquists).

1420: the first fighting. Žižka 'defeated Catholics at Sudoměř (25 March 1420)'; Pope Martin V's bull of 17 March 1420 proclaims a crusade; Sigismund arrives before Prague on 30 June and is defeated at Vítkov Hill (July) and Pankrác (1 November).
25 January 1437: 'by mutual agreement with Sigismund, Tábor was promoted to royal town'.
25 January 1437: Tábor becomes a royal town of King Sigismund's Bohemia.
January 1437: the Hussite state ends with Tábor's agreement with Sigismund; the Utraquist church continues inside the Kingdom of Bohemia under the Compacts.

wars.name: Hussite Wars
wars.outcome: Five crusades (1420, 1421, 1422, 1427, 1431) failed; Žižka's and Prokop's armies raided Silesia, Saxony, Lusatia, Hungary and Meissen; the Taborite army was annihilated at Lipany on 30 May 1434; the Compacts were signed at Jihlava on 5 July 1436.

certainty.note: No page draws the Hussite lands as a boundary; the unions were held by towns and castles ('Landfrieden of Plzeň' for the loyalists), so the frontiers are approximate.
